generic_name: Desogestrel, Ethinyl Estradiol, and Ethinyl Estradiol
drug_class: Combination Hormonal Contraceptive (Biphasic Oral Contraceptive Pill)
purpose: This medication is a birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also help make your periods more regular, reduce menstrual cramps, and decrease the amount of bleeding during your period. Some forms may also help with acne.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — a progestin called desogestrel and an estrogen called ethinyl estradiol — that work together to prevent pregnancy. They stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month, thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm cannot reach an egg, and thin the lining of your uterus. All three of these actions together make it very hard to get pregnant.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headaches, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods (especially in the first few months), mood changes, decreased sex drive, and bloating. These often improve after the first 2-3 months.
warnings: Do not smoke while taking this pill, especially if you are over 35 years old, as it raises your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver disease, or certain cancers. This pill does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have chest pain, severe headache, vision changes, or leg pain or swelling.
typical_dosing: You take one pill by mouth every day at the same time each day for 28 days, then start a new pack. The pack contains active hormone pills and a short phase of low-dose estrogen-only pills, followed by reminder pills. Try to take it at the same time every day to make it work best. If you miss a pill, follow the instructions in your package or call your pharmacist.
